passage: Chaitanya, you asked what actually helped, so I'm Ujjwal and I'll be practical. I did three small things in one afternoon. First, I muted her accounts. Not blocked, not an announcement, just quiet. I did not want a scene. Second, I moved all our photos into a folder called "later", not deleted, just out of sight. Third, my usual route to class went past her department, so I started walking around by the library. It added six minutes. No one knew, and I did not tell anyone. It felt slightly silly, like arranging a room so you don't keep bumping into the same chair. But my mornings stopped starting with a jab. Space to heal, I found, is mostly not seeing things.

passage:
I'm Kishore, Chinmay's roommate. I noticed the changes before he explained them.
The first was his phone. The day after the breakup, I saw him scroll to her name, pause, and tap 'mute'. Not block. Just mute. He did the same on two other apps.
The second was his laptop. That evening he made a folder called 'Later' and dragged in every photo of the two of them, the Goa trip, the farewell party, the one on his desktop too. He replaced the background with plain blue.
The third surprised me. He started leaving ten minutes earlier for class, walking the long way round behind the canteen instead of past the girls' hostel.
When I asked, he said, 'I'm not angry at her. I just need less of her around for a while.'
I can't say how much it helped inside, but by the end of the month he was sleeping properly again.

qa.q: What did Chinmay name the folder of photos?
What does 'I'm not angry at her. I just need less of her around' suggest about Chinmay?
qa.a: He still feels hurt but not bitter, and wants space to heal without any confrontation.

qa.q: What else could Chinmay add if reminders still catch him off guard?
qa.a: Plan time with a friend or an activity for the hours when reminders hit hardest, like evenings, so the space he made is filled with something good.

qa.q: How do the changes look to Kishore?
qa.a: Kishore notices each small step before hearing the reason, and sees Chinmay sleeping properly again by the end of the month.
